explain: _vident_ is 3rd person plural (present tense) of _videō_ (“they see”). The ending tells the person: -ō = I, -s = you, -t = he or she, -mus = we, -tis = you all, -nt = they. _discipulum_ is accusative singular, the object, so it does not change.
distractors: Avem vident.
_avem_ means “bird”, so this says “They see a bird”.
Discipulus vident.
_discipulus_ is nominative singular, but it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative: _discipulum_.
Discipulum videt.
_videt_ is 3rd person singular (present tense) of _videō_ (“he sees”). That would say “He sees a pupil” instead of “They see a pupil”.

explain: _vidētis_ is 2nd person plural (present tense) of _videō_ (“you all see”). The ending tells the person: -ō = I, -s = you, -t = he or she, -mus = we, -tis = you all, -nt = they. _discipulum_ is accusative singular, the object, so it does not change.
distractors: Discipulus vidētis.
_discipulus_ is nominative singular, but it is the object (the thing acted on), so it stays accusative: _discipulum_.
Diem vidētis.
_diem_ means “day”, so this says “You all see a day”.
Discipulum videō.
_videō_ is 1st person singular (present tense) of _videō_ (“I see”). That would say “I see a pupil” instead of “You all see a pupil”.
